subtopicTitle: INS error propagation — error state equations

cards.front: What is the role of error-state equations in an INS?
cards.back: They provide a linearized time-varying model of how small errors in position, velocity, attitude and sensor biases propagate due to the nonlinear strapdown kinematics and Earth-rate effects.

cards.front: Name the five core error states used in a basic INS error-state vector.
cards.back: δr (position), δv (velocity), φ (attitude/tilt), b_a (accelerometer bias), b_g (gyro bias).

cards.front: State the attitude-error differential equation (inertial frame).
Give the velocity-error equation including Coriolis and gravity terms.
How does a constant gyro bias b_g propagate into attitude error?
cards.back: Attitude error grows linearly: $\phi(t) = \phi(0) + b_g t$ (neglecting Earth-rate coupling).

cards.front: Derive the second-order position-error dynamics that produce Schuler oscillation.
cards.back: Differentiate velocity error twice and substitute attitude error: $\delta\ddot{r} + \omega_s^2\delta r = 0$ where $\omega_s = \sqrt{g/R}\approx0.00124$ rad/s.

cards.front: What is the effect of accelerometer bias on horizontal position error after long time?
cards.back: Position error grows as $\frac12 b_a t^2$ modulated by bounded Schuler oscillation; unbounded quadratic growth dominates.
